id: title:DanielVisca:stop exposing observed timestamp in hogql metrics tables

observations.behavior: Removes the 'observed_timestamp' field and its associated DateTimeDatabaseField definition from MetricsTable.
observations.posthog_connection: Changes the database schema for stored metric records; this could affect downstream queries or ingestion expectations if dependent on that specific retention-boundary field.

observations.posthog_connection: Preserves existing behavior while removing an unused or redundant field, potentially reducing storage overhead without changing query results.

observations.behavior: Deletes mapping entry for observed_timestamp in backend metrics4_samples.py, aligning with schema change.
observations.posthog_connection: Supports backend compatibility after schema removal; no longer expects observed_timestamp data when processing samples.

observations.limitations: Only four hunks provided across three files; broader context not available. No tests demonstrate runtime behavior or migration handling. No release notes or adoption indicators are supplied.

review.limitations: Only four hunks provided across three files; broader context not available. No tests demonstrate runtime behavior or migration handling. No release notes or adoption indicators are supplied.
review.reason: The changes remove a single optional metadata column and update related mappings and one test. The implementation is bounded: it removes a field from two tables and its usage in the sample-processing layer. While this could reduce storage and simplify queries, there's no evidence of systemic benefit or risk reduction beyond local cleanup. Tier 2 fits because the change is substantive but localized; tier 3 requires broader capability improvement demonstrated across components.
review.posthog_relevance: Removes stored ingestion-time metadata that may have been unnecessary given current retention policies. Could help users by slightly lowering warehouse costs if previously retained per-record timestamps were not used elsewhere.
review.uncertainty: Without seeing dependent query execution or migration scripts, cannot assess whether removing observed_timestamp breaks existing dashboards or alert conditions.
